feature_name: --up and --down are mutually exclusive
user_story: As a user, I want the CLI to reject combining `--up` and `--down` so that I get a clear usage error instead of ambiguous behavior.
expected_behaviour: BUG FOUND & FIXED (this QA pass): --up/--down conflict was previously caught entirely by a declarative `#[arg(conflicts_with = "down")]` / `conflicts_with = "up"` pair inside clap's own parser (src/cli.rs), so the user saw clap's terse "cannot be used with" text and exit code 2 -- never the four-line E1002 `ERROR [E1002] CONFLICTING_DIRECTION: ...` block that `--man` explicitly documents for this exact error (man.rs ERRORS section, E1002 entry). Fixed: the declarative `conflicts_with` attributes were removed from both `up` and `down` (src/cli.rs); `Cli::direction_conflict()` checks `up.is_some() && down.is_some()` and `main()` emits `errors::E1002.report(...).emit()` before `Cli::validate()` or any other dispatch runs (src/main.rs), so the actual stderr output now matches the documented four-line block.
how_to_test: Run `resume --up 1 --down 2` and confirm exit code 2 with stderr starting `ERROR [E1002] CONFLICTING_DIRECTION:` and containing Trigger:/Fix:/Example: lines, matching `resume --man`'s E1002 section exactly.
error_notes: Fixed and regression-tested 2026-08-23. Unit test updated: direction_conflict_is_no_longer_a_parse_error (src/cli.rs) asserts parsing succeeds and Cli::direction_conflict() is true. New real-binary integration test: direction_conflict_prints_the_e1002_four_line_block (tests/step9_app.rs) asserts the compiled binary's stderr matches the documented four-line block. Full `make test` (497 tests across all suites) and `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings` both clean after the fix. Also resolves the cli-error-catalog-mechanics KEY ASYMMETRY note for E1002 specifically (E1001/E1003 remain intentionally parser-hint-wrapped, matching their man page 'Message:' field, which is a separate, correct-as-documented design, not a bug).

feature_name: Scope base and Workspace candidates are canonicalized (symlinks resolved)
user_story: As a user, I want resume to compare real (symlink-resolved) paths so that a symlinked path to my project matches sessions recorded under the real path.

feature_name: A missing/nonexistent base directory is a usage error
user_story: As a user, I want a clear error if I pass a directory that does not exist so that I don't get a confusing crash.

It now canonicalizes then rejects non-directories with InvalidInput and the message `base path <path> is not a directory`; symlinks to directories remain accepted. Verified via `cargo test --lib scope::tests --locked` (18 passed) and a live run: `resume README.md --list -a pi` exits 2 with `resume: base path README.md is not a directory`.

Fixed: non-Supported sessions now append a visible `[DiscoverOnly]`/`[Unavailable]`/`[Unsupported]` label to picker/list rows and include `SUPPORT <status>` in Preview (src/app.rs:918-967); JSON retains `support: "Unavailable"` unchanged, and the existing E3003 selection guard remains authoritative. Verified via `cargo test --lib app::tests --locked` (14 passed, including picker_row_and_preview_mark_non_supported_sessions) and a live fixture with its recorded Pi workspace removed, rendering `[Unavailable]`.

feature_name: --config explicit path has highest precedence
user_story: As a user, I want an explicit `--config <PATH>` to always win over XDG/home discovery, even if the path doesn't exist yet.
expected_behaviour: `discover_path` returns `explicit` immediately whenever `Some`, before checking XDG or home (src/config.rs:67-70 (discover_path explicit return)), tested by `explicit_then_xdg_then_home_precedence` (src/config.rs:112 (explicit_then_xdg_then_home_precedence)); if the explicit file doesn't exist, `load_path` will fail with `ConfigError::Read` when actually loading (src/config.rs:99-107 (load_path)).

feature_name: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/resume/config.toml precedence over home
user_story: As a user, I want my XDG_CONFIG_HOME config to be used when present, ahead of the ~/.config fallback.
expected_behaviour: `discover_path` checks `xdg.join("resume/config.toml")` via the injected `exists` predicate and returns it if present, before falling back to `home.join(".config/resume/config.toml")` (src/config.rs:71-78 (discover_path xdg check)), tested by `explicit_then_xdg_then_home_precedence` (src/config.rs:112 (explicit_then_xdg_then_home_precedence)).
how_to_test: Create both `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/resume/config.toml` and `~/.config/resume/config.toml` with different `agents` lists, run `resume --list` with no `--config`, and confirm the XDG file's settings apply.

feature_name: ~/.config/resume/config.toml is used only when XDG config is absent
user_story: As a user without XDG_CONFIG_HOME configured (or without a resume config under it), I want resume to fall back to ~/.config/resume/config.toml.
expected_behaviour: `discover_path` only returns the home path when the XDG path (if any) does not exist per the `exists` predicate (src/config.rs:79-81 (discover_path home fallback)), tested by `explicit_then_xdg_then_home_precedence` (src/config.rs:112 (explicit_then_xdg_then_home_precedence)).
how_to_test: Unset XDG_CONFIG_HOME (or ensure no resume config exists under it), create only `~/.config/resume/config.toml`, and confirm `resume --list` applies its settings.

feature_name: Exactly one config file is loaded; files are never merged
user_story: As a user, I want resume to load a single config file deterministically rather than silently merging multiple sources, so config behavior is predictable.
expected_behaviour: `discover_path` returns the first matching path by precedence and `load` loads only that one file via `load_path` (src/config.rs:67-81 (discover_path returns first match)); README.md's Configuration section states 'Exactly one file is loaded; files are not merged.'
how_to_test: Create differing config.toml files at explicit/XDG/home locations and confirm only the highest-precedence one's fields take effect, with no merged fields from the others.

feature_name: Unknown TOML fields are rejected
user_story: As a user, I want a typo'd config field (e.g. from an old or unsupported option) to fail loudly rather than being silently ignored.
expected_behaviour: `Config` derives `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` (src/config.rs:36 (#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)])), so any field not in {agents, confirm_always, preview, preview_position, verbose} causes `toml::from_str` to fail, surfaced as `ConfigError::Parse`, tested by `unknown_and_invalid_fields_are_rejected` for `mystery = true` (src/config.rs:136-152 (unknown_and_invalid_fields_are_rejected) + :158 (parse_error_message_includes_line_and_field_detail)).
how_to_test: Write a config.toml containing `mystery = true`, run `resume --config <that file> --list`, and confirm it fails with a usage error rather than silently ignoring the field.
error_notes: 2026-08-23 audit: strict unknown-field rejection remains correct, but the stated accepted-field set omitted valid `since`. `Config` has six optional fields: agents, since, confirm_always, preview, preview_position, verbose (src/config.rs:37-45).

feature_name: Invalid enum/type values in config are rejected
user_story: As a user, I want an invalid `preview_position` or `preview` value to fail clearly instead of silently falling back to a default.
expected_behaviour: `PreviewMode`/`PreviewPosition` derive `Deserialize` with `#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]` and only accept `hidden`/`visible` or `auto`/`right`/`bottom` respectively (src/config.rs:22-25 (PreviewMode), :29-33 (PreviewPosition)); an invalid value like `preview_position = 'left'` fails `toml::from_str`, tested by `unknown_and_invalid_fields_are_rejected` (src/config.rs:136-152 (unknown_and_invalid_fields_are_rejected)).
how_to_test: Write a config.toml with `preview_position = 'left'`, run `resume --config <that file> --list`, and confirm it fails with a parse/usage error.

feature_name: Config-level 'since' field accepts the same duration|date|all syntax as --since
user_story: As a user, I want to set a default `since` cutoff in config.toml so I don't have to pass --since on every invocation, and have --since on the CLI override it when I do.
expected_behaviour: `Config.since: Option<Since>` deserializes via `deserialize_since`, reusing `Since::from_str` so config and CLI accept identical syntax and reject the same malformed inputs (src/config.rs); `effective_options` prefers `cli.since` over `config.since` when both are present (src/app.rs), mirroring the -a/--agent override pattern.
how_to_test: Write a config.toml with `since = '7d'`, run `resume --config <path> --list` with no --since flag and confirm the 7-day cutoff applies; run again with `--since all` on the CLI and confirm it overrides the config value; covered by `documented_field_set_loads`/`since_all_and_date_load_from_config` in src/config.rs.

feature_name: The full documented field set loads and applies correctly
user_story: As a user, I want every field shown in `resume config example` (agents, confirm_always, verbose, preview, preview_position) to actually parse and take effect together.

feature_name: Settings-driven agent selection when neither -a nor config.agents is set
user_story: As a user without -a or config.agents, I want resume to use my saved setup selection, and on a first noninteractive list/json run receive a setup hint instead of silently scanning every integration.
expected_behaviour: `effective_options` takes `settings.agents()` when `cli.agent` is empty and `config.agents` is None (src/app.rs:172-181); it does not hard-code four agents. `Settings::default()` derives its selection from all five `SUPPORTED_AGENTS` names (src/settings.rs:68-71; src/cli.rs:96), while an absent settings file on --list/--json exits with the setup requirement before effective_options runs (src/app.rs:105-121).

With no CLI `-a` and no TOML `agents`, it takes `settings.agents()` (src/app.rs:172-181); for `--list`/`--json`, absent settings require interactive `resume setup` rather than discovering immediately (src/app.rs:105-121). `Settings::default()` derives its catalog from `SUPPORTED_AGENTS`, which includes five names (src/settings.rs, src/cli.rs:96).

user_story: As a user, I want Ctrl-R to do nothing rather than accidentally triggering a filesystem scan, since Skim's default `reload` action would run `find` on the working directory when items come from a channel.
expected_behaviour: `build_options`/`build_production_options` bind `"ctrl-r:ignore"` (src/picker.rs:255-267 (build_options, FINDING comment), :418 (production)) instead of `reload`; the code comment documents the FINDING that channel-fed Skim's `reload` without an argument re-runs the default `find` command, which is unacceptable, and the accepted fallback is the dual-section preview; regression-tested by `ctrl_r_does_not_scan_filesystem` (tests/picker_spike.rs (ctrl_r_does_not_scan_filesystem)).

user_story: As a user, I want to press Esc to back out of the picker cleanly without resuming any session, restoring my terminal.
expected_behaviour: Both `build_options` and `build_production_options` bind `"esc:abort"`; `classify` maps an abort outcome whose final key is not Ctrl-C to `PickerOutcome::Cancelled` (src/picker.rs:309-313 (classify abort arm)); `run_interactive` maps `Cancelled` to `EXIT_OK` (0) unless zero sessions/integrations succeeded, in which case `EXIT_ERROR` (src/app.rs:287-295); regression-tested by `esc_cancels_and_restores_terminal` asserting exit 0 (tests/picker_spike.rs:338).

feature_name: Ctrl-C interrupts the picker, exit code 130
user_story: As a user, I want Ctrl-C to interrupt the picker distinctly from Esc, using the conventional SIGINT-style exit code 130, so scripts can detect a hard interrupt.
expected_behaviour: `classify` checks `is_interrupt(&output.final_key)` which matches `SkimKey::Ctrl('c')` and returns `PickerOutcome::Interrupted` (src/picker.rs:310-311 (classify) + :342-344 (is_interrupt)); `run_interactive` maps `Interrupted` directly to `EXIT_INTERRUPT` = 130 (src/app.rs:33 (EXIT_INTERRUPT const) + :296 (Interrupted arm)); regression-tested by `ctrl_c_exits_130` (tests/picker_spike.rs:357).

feature_name: Terminal smaller than 60x10 fails preflight before picker starts
user_story: As a user with an undersized terminal window, I want resume to fail with a clear error before Skim even attempts to render, rather than crashing or rendering garbled output.
expected_behaviour: `preflight()` reads terminal size via ioctl `TIOCGWINSZ` on `/dev/tty` and returns `Err("terminal too small: WxH (minimum 60x10)")` when `w < MIN_TERM_WIDTH (60) || h < MIN_TERM_HEIGHT (10)` (src/picker.rs:436-457, size guard at 451-455; constants at src/picker.rs:44-45); `run_interactive` surfaces this as `PickerOutcome::PreflightFailed`, printed to stderr, mapped to `EXIT_USAGE` (2) at src/app.rs:297-303 — the same exit code (2) the standalone spike example uses, so there is no production/spike discrepancy.
how_to_test: Resize a terminal (or spawn a PTY) to 40 columns x 8 rows, run `resume` interactively, and confirm it fails fast with a 'terminal too small' message and exit code 2 rather than attempting to render.
error_notes: BUG FOUND & FIXED 2026-08-11: PickerOutcome::PreflightFailed was mapped to exit 1 (EXIT_ERROR), sharing a match arm with InternalError; docs/product-design.md §5 'Terminal behavior' requires exit 2 for a too-small terminal. Fixed: PreflightFailed now maps to EXIT_USAGE (2), split from InternalError (src/app.rs run_interactive).

feature_name: No controlling terminal (/dev/tty unavailable) fails preflight
user_story: As a user running resume in a context with no TTY (e.g. certain CI/automation contexts), I want a clear preflight failure rather than a confusing panic.

Regression: tests/step9_app.rs::no_controlling_terminal_is_a_usage_error_with_a_list_json_suggestion.

user_story: As a user piping data into resume's stdin for another purpose, I want the interactive picker to still work because it talks to /dev/tty directly, not fd 0.

feature_name: Non-verbose diagnostics aggregate same-category occurrences into one summed count
user_story: As a user, I want repeated diagnostics of the same category (e.g. many skipped Claude files) to render as a single 'category: N' line instead of N duplicate lines, so stderr stays readable.
expected_behaviour: `aggregate_diagnostics(errors, verbose=false)` groups purely by `category` (ignoring path/chain) via `aggregate_by(errors, |e| (e.category, None, None))`, summing counts into one entry per category (src/app.rs:892-931); `render_diagnostic` in non-verbose mode prints only `resume: <category>: <count>` (src/app.rs:933-951); this is the exact behavior added by the current HEAD commit 64e4cf2 (historical; behavior now further hardened by the M2 fix making print_diagnostics unconditional) 'fix: aggregate same-category diagnostics into one summed count in non-verbose mode', regression-tested by `non_verbose_diagnostics_collapse_by_category_summing_counts` which feeds 3 distinct-path claude_no_session_id diagnostics and 1 pi_skipped diagnostic, asserting exactly 2 collapsed lines with counts 3 and 2 (src/app.rs:963-1008).
how_to_test: Craft fixtures producing 3 separate claude_no_session_id-triggering transcripts and run `resume --list` (non-verbose); confirm stderr shows exactly one line 'resume: claude_no_session_id: 3', not three separate lines.

feature_name: Verbose diagnostics preserve distinct per-path entries while merging exact duplicates
user_story: As a user diagnosing a discovery problem with --verbose, I want to see one line per distinct problematic file/path, not one blob per category, so I can find and fix the specific file.
expected_behaviour: `aggregate_diagnostics(errors, verbose=true)` groups by the full `(category, verbose_path, verbose_chain)` tuple, so distinct paths remain separate lines while exact duplicates (same category+path+chain) are merged and summed (src/app.rs:892-900), regression-tested by `verbose_diagnostics_keep_distinct_paths_but_merge_exact_duplicates`, which asserts 2 distinct paths remain separate while a true duplicate of path 'one.jsonl' is merged into a count of 2 (src/app.rs:1010-1033).
how_to_test: Craft fixtures producing errors on 2 distinct claude transcript paths plus one exact duplicate error, run `resume --verbose --list`, and confirm stderr shows 2 lines, with the duplicated path's line showing count 2.

feature_name: Verbose diagnostic output redacts URLs, remotes, and base64-like blobs
user_story: As a user sharing verbose diagnostic output for troubleshooting, I want URLs, git remotes, and long base64-looking blobs stripped from the path/chain text so I don't leak secrets.
expected_behaviour: `render_diagnostic` in verbose mode calls `redact_path`/`redact_text` (from `crate::diagnostics`) on `verbose_path`/`verbose_chain` before formatting the stderr line (src/app.rs:933-951); `redact_text` replaces `https://`/`http://`/`ssh://`/`git://`/`file://`/`ftp://` URLs with `[redacted-url]`, `git@host:...` remotes with `[redacted-remote]`, and 40+ char base64-alphabet runs with `[redacted-blob]` (src/diagnostics.rs:135-180), regression-tested end-to-end by `verbose_diagnostic_output_is_redacted` (src/app.rs:1035-1049) and at the unit level by `redact_text_removes_urls`/`redact_text_removes_git_remote`/`redact_text_removes_base64_blobs` (src/diagnostics.rs:184-215).
how_to_test: Force a diagnostic whose verbose_chain embeds a secret URL (e.g. https://secret.example/api) and run `resume --verbose --list`; confirm stderr contains '[redacted-url]' and never the literal domain.
error_notes: Phase 4 independent re-test: focused end-to-end/unit redaction tests passed (URL, git remote, and 40+ character blob are replaced and originals absent); full all-features suite also passed.

feature_name: Diagnostics never include session message bodies
user_story: As a user, I want diagnostic output to never accidentally echo the private content of my session transcripts.
expected_behaviour: `Diagnostic.verbose_chain` is always a short, static/derived description string set by integration code (e.g. "no embedded sessionId and no cwd; skipped"), never raw message text (src/integration/claude/discover.rs (diagnostic_chain call sites, split out of mod.rs)); `no_message_body_leaks_in_normal_mode` test explicitly asserts a chain containing 'password'/'hunter2' does not leak through normal-mode rendering, which only prints category+count (src/diagnostics.rs:273 (no_message_body_leaks_in_normal_mode)).

It now replaces whole matching lines with `[redacted-message]` before URL, remote, and blob redaction. Verified via `cargo test --lib diagnostics::tests --locked` (11 passed).

feature_name: --list with zero sessions found prints nothing to stdout and exits 0
user_story: As a user in a directory with no discoverable sessions, I want a clean empty result and success exit code, not an error, so scripting `resume --list | wc -l` behaves predictably.
expected_behaviour: CORRECTED: `--list` with zero sessions found does NOT print nothing — `print_list` (src/app.rs:856-869) calls `empty_list_message`, which returns `Some("No Sessions found in Scope.")` when records is empty, so stdout gets exactly that one line, not zero lines (`resume --list | wc -l` yields 1, not 0). `discovery_exit` (src/app.rs:953-958) still returns `EXIT_OK` (0) unless zero sessions AND zero successful integrations.
how_to_test: Run `resume --list` in a temp HOME with valid-but-empty agent roots and confirm stdout is exactly 'No Sessions found in Scope.' with exit 0 (unit-tested by `empty_list_has_human_readable_fallback`, src/app.rs:967; no end-to-end --list test currently asserts this exact stdout content — E2E gap).
error_notes: Corrected by the Diagnostics/Output/ExitCode domain audit: original 'prints nothing to stdout' was inaccurate.

feature_name: --list exits with an error only when every integration fails outright
user_story: As a user, I want resume to distinguish 'no sessions found' (success) from 'every integration failed to even run' (error), so I can tell a real problem from an empty result.
expected_behaviour: `discovery_exit` returns `EXIT_ERROR` (1) specifically when `records.is_empty() && state.successful_integrations.load(...) == 0`, i.e. zero integrations even completed successfully, not merely zero sessions found (src/app.rs:953-958); `AgentDiscovery::failed` marks `integration_ok: false` on root-resolution failure (e.g. `pi_root_unavailable`) (src/app.rs:358).
how_to_test: Force all four agent roots to be unresolvable (e.g. by pointing every agent env var at a location resolution can't handle) and confirm `resume --list` exits 1 with diagnostics explaining each integration's failure category.

feature_name: One failing integration does not block sessions from the others
user_story: As a user, I want a broken/misconfigured integration (e.g. corrupted Codex root) to still let pi/claude/omp sessions come through, isolated as a diagnostic rather than aborting the whole run.
expected_behaviour: `discover_all`/`run_interactive` spawn one independent thread per agent via `discover_agent`; each thread's `AgentDiscovery` (records + errors + integration_ok) is aggregated independently into shared `DiscoveryState`/`records` (src/app.rs:193-232 (discover_all), 234-308 (run_interactive)); a single agent's `AgentDiscovery::failed(category)` only contributes a diagnostic entry, never aborts other threads' results.
how_to_test: Break only the Codex integration (e.g. set CODEX_HOME to an unreadable/garbage path) while pi/claude/omp fixtures remain valid, run `resume --list`, and confirm pi/claude/omp sessions still appear alongside a codex_root_unavailable (or similar) diagnostic on stderr.

feature_name: JSON output is exactly the v1 envelope {schemaVersion, sessions, errors}
user_story: As a tool author consuming `resume --json`, I want a stable top-level envelope with schemaVersion, sessions array, and errors array, and nothing else, so I can parse it reliably.
expected_behaviour: `JsonOutput` derives `Serialize` with fields `schema_version` (renamed `schemaVersion`, always `1`), `sessions: Vec<JsonSession>`, `errors: Vec<JsonError>` (src/app.rs:791-797); docs/json-schema.md's JSON Schema pins `required: [schemaVersion, sessions, errors]` and `additionalProperties: false` at the top level.

feature_name: JSON session objects contain exactly agent, profile, id, title, workspace, support, activity, risk
user_story: As a tool author, I want each session object in the JSON output to have a stable, complete field set with predictable null-vs-string semantics.
expected_behaviour: `JsonSession` has exactly `agent, profile, id, title, workspace, support, activity, risk` (src/app.rs:799-808); `profile`/`title`/`workspace` become JSON `null` via `Option` fields when absent; `support`/`activity`/`risk` are rendered via `format!("{:?}", ...)` (Rust Debug form), explicitly documented in docs/json-schema.md as NOT lower-case enums (e.g. an Active session's activity string can embed its observed_at timestamp).

feature_name: JSON error objects contain only category and count (no verbose path/chain)
user_story: As a tool author, I want the JSON `errors` array to expose only a safe, redacted summary — never the verbose per-path diagnostic detail that stays on stderr.

Never includes `verbose_path`/`verbose_chain`.

Dedicated multi-category parity test added: json_errors_aggregate_counts_match_stderr_across_multiple_categories (tests/step9_app.rs) forces 2 codex_invalid_session + 2 claude_no_session_id diagnostics in one run and asserts each collapses to one JSON errors[] entry with count 2, matching stderr's 'category: 2' lines -- closing the multi-category E2E gap. Prior incidental single-category coverage (codex_corrupt_rollout_is_diagnosed_while_valid_sibling_survives) remains.

feature_name: JSON output omits full/raw message bodies while title may contain a bounded user-message excerpt
user_story: As a user, I want `resume --json` to omit full/raw conversation transcripts while clearly warning that Session titles may contain a bounded excerpt derived from my first message.

feature_name: Exit code 0 on success (session resumed after prompt cancel, or list/json completes, or Esc)

NOT ALL exit-2 paths use the catalog — unknown-agent and missing-directory still print bare messages (E1005/E3004 reserved-not-wired by design).

user_story: As a Pi user, I want resume's exact resume command to match Pi's own safest resume mechanism, using the transcript path rather than a possibly-ambiguous ID flag.

feature_name: Pi session title precedence: session_info.name, else summary of first human message
user_story: As a Pi user, I want the picker to show a meaningful title for each session, preferring an explicit name Pi set, falling back to a summary of what I actually typed.

feature_name: Pi Active status requires validated stable-ID + transcript-path association; absence is Unknown, never Inactive
user_story: As a Pi user, I want resume to only claim a session is Active when it has real corroborating evidence (matching session-control ID and path), never guess based on process presence alone.

feature_name: Pi sessions get BroadWorkspace risk when recorded cwd is $HOME or /
user_story: As a Pi user, I want a pi session recorded against my entire home directory to be flagged risky, same as other integrations.

Citation update (2026-08-11 real-binary QA pass): Internal ResolutionInputs precedence (profile_flag > OMP_PROFILE > PI_PROFILE) is correctly implemented at roots.rs:125-144, but `profile_flag` is reserved/non-CLI — `resume` currently has NO --profile flag (src/cli.rs:252-318 has no such option; `resume --json --agent omp --profile personal` exits 2 'unexpected argument'). The row's verification instruction presenting --profile as user-invocable is inaccurate; only OMP_PROFILE/PI_PROFILE env vars are actually reachable from the CLI today.

feature_name: OMP Active status requires a genuine two-stage positive-evidence pipeline with a real staleness gate (M3 fix)
user_story: As an OMP user, I want resume to only claim Active when it has strong, multi-signal evidence (not just a leftover breadcrumb file from a closed terminal).
expected_behaviour: OMP Active is a two-stage positive-evidence pipeline. Stage 1 (`correlate_live_with`, src/integration/omp/activity.rs:169-211): for each terminal breadcrumb it requires (a) a live OMP process on that TTY via `ProcessTable::live_on_tty`, (b) a breadcrumb `recorded_at` (file mtime), and (c) a FRESHNESS GATE — `fresh = recorded_at >= process.started_at` when the process start time is known (activity.rs:183-184); when `started_at` is unavailable it falls back to a 12h window (`now - recorded_at <= BREADCRUMB_FRESHNESS`, :192-193) AND emits an `OMP_BREADCRUMB_START_TIME_UNAVAILABLE` diagnostic so the unknown is visible, never silent. A breadcrumb older than the recycled-TTY process, or older than 12h with no start time, is REJECTED before any evidence is recorded. Stage 2 (`activity_status`/`ActivityEvidence::matches`, activity.rs:19-54): only evidence produced by stage 1 (live_process=true, tty=Some, breadcrumb_alive=true, matching canonical session path) maps to Active; everything else is Unknown. A stale breadcrumb alone can NEVER reach Active because stage 1 never emits evidence for it.
how_to_test: Feed `correlate_live_with` a breadcrumb whose `recorded_at` is older than the live process `started_at` and assert the evidence map is empty (`correlate_live_rejects_breadcrumb_older_than_recycled_tty_process`, src/integration/omp/tests/activity.rs:75). Feed a process with `started_at=None` and a breadcrumb just inside/exactly at the 12h `BREADCRUMB_FRESHNESS` boundary and assert Active + one `OMP_BREADCRUMB_START_TIME_UNAVAILABLE` diagnostic; push `recorded_at` 1s past the boundary and assert empty (`missing_process_start_time_uses_twelve_hour_freshness_fallback`, activity.rs:108). Also assert full positive evidence -> Active and any single missing signal -> Unknown (`correlate_live_requires_process_tty_breadcrumb_and_existing_transcript` :37; `activity_active_only_with_live_process_tty_and_matching_breadcrumb` :227).
error_notes: REWRITTEN — the original row described only the CONSUMER of activity evidence (matches requires live_process+tty+breadcrumb_alive) which was the pre-M3 tautological gate flagged by docs/review/post-merge-review.md finding M3 (a recycled TTY could falsely report Active). The producer-side staleness gate is now real; see the dedicated omp-active-staleness-gate-m3-fix row for the specific exploit-closure evidence.

feature_name: Three-layer help design (-h short / --help full reference / --man manual)
user_story: As a user, I want graduated help depth — a one-screen orientation with -h, a full flag reference with --help, and the complete manual with --man — so I get the right detail for my need without drowning.
expected_behaviour: Implemented via clap's `#[command(...)]` attributes on `Cli` (src/cli.rs ~207-247): `about` feeds `-h`; `long_about` (multi-paragraph) feeds `--help`; `after_help` (SYNTAX+EXAMPLES, ending with a pointer to `--help`/`--man`) feeds the `-h` footer; `after_long_help` (COMMON EXAMPLES + COMMON ERRORS listing E1001-E1004/E3001-E3003 + SEE ALSO pointing to --man) feeds the `--help` footer. Per-arg, only `help` is set (never `long_help`), keeping the `--help` option column scannable; long prose lives only in the man page. clap's rule: when `long_about`/`after_long_help` are set, `--help` uses them and `-h` falls back to `about`/`after_help`. The layering is documented in docs/design/cli-help-layers-plan.md §2 with a strict-subset rule (L1 subset-of L2 subset-of L3).
how_to_test: Run `resume -h` (one screen, ends with pointer to --help/--man); run `resume --help` (longer, per-arg help strings, COMMON ERRORS block); run `resume --man` (full manual). Confirm L1 is a strict subset of L2 which is a strict subset of L3.
error_notes: E2E GAP: help_describes_every_option (src/cli.rs:391) renders ONLY render_long_help() (the --help layer). No test renders render_help() (the -h layer) to assert it is strictly shorter and uses about/after_help not long_about/after_long_help. The strict-subset invariant is documented but not automated. Also no test asserts the COMMON ERRORS block lists exactly the seven catalog codes. Citation update (2026-08-11 real-binary QA pass): Replace src/cli.rs ~207-247 with src/cli.rs:160-250; the described layering is verified (strict-subset test remains at 412-432).

feature_name: Unified E-code error catalog (E1001-E1004/E3001-E3003) — single source of truth, selectively wired
user_story: As a user/debugger, I want stable E-codes (E1001 INVALID_SINCE ... E3003 WORKSPACE_UNAVAILABLE) with consistent trigger/fix/example text across stderr, --help, and --man, so I can grep/Google a code and get an actionable remedy.
expected_behaviour: `src/errors.rs` defines `CATALOG: [ErrorSpec; 7]` as the single source; `Report::emit()` writes a four-line block (`ERROR [Exxxx] SLUG: <what>` / `Trigger:` / `Fix:` / `Example:`) to stderr and returns the exit code. Wiring is PARTIAL and indirect: E1001 (INVALID_SINCE) and E1003 (INVALID_DISTANCE) are wired only as the parser-hint STRING (cli.rs:49,21 via `.parser_message()`), wrapped in clap's own value-parse error format — the four-line block is NOT emitted for these. E1002 (CONFLICTING_DIRECTION) has NO runtime emit site at all — the --up/--down mutual exclusion is enforced by clap's `conflicts_with` attribute, which emits clap's generic ArgumentConflict text instead. E1004 (INVALID_CONFIG) IS wired via the four-line block (app.rs:98-104). E1005 (UNKNOWN_AGENT) and E3004 (DIRECTORY_UNREADABLE) are RESERVED but not wired by design (errors.rs doc comment lines 15-18) — those paths still print bare `resume: <message>`. main.rs has ZERO errors:: references; Cli::validate() (cli.rs:346-369) uses plain clap ArgumentConflict text with no E-code for the --list/--json+confirm and config/completions+query rejections.
how_to_test: `resume --up 1 --down 2` (exit 2, clap conflict text — NOT the E1002 four-line block); `resume --since yesterday` (exit 2, message contains the E1001 parser-hint string); `resume --up -1` (exit 2, E1003 hint string); `resume --config /bad.toml --list` (exit 2, four-line E1004 block); `resume --list --confirm-always` (exit 2, clap ArgumentConflict plain text, no E-code).
error_notes: KEY ASYMMETRY (E1002 portion FIXED this QA pass, see cli-up-down-conflict): the four-line Report block used to be emitted ONLY from app.rs (E1004, E3003); the man page (man.rs E1002 entry) implied a matching block for --up/--down conflicts, but that path was fully absorbed by clap's own declarative `conflicts_with`, which never called into resume's error catalog. Fixed: `Cli::direction_conflict()` + `main.rs` now emit the real E1002 `Report` before any other validation runs (src/cli.rs, src/main.rs). E1001 (INVALID_SINCE) and E1003 (INVALID_DISTANCE) remain intentionally wired through clap's own value-parse error path using `parser_message()` (a short hint string), NOT the four-line block -- this matches the man page, which documents an extra 'Message:' field only for those two codes, distinguishing them from the four-line-block codes (E1002/E1004/E3001-E3003) by design, not by omission. Tests: errors.rs unit tests pin catalog internal consistency; man.rs:629 pins man<->catalog sync; direction_conflict_prints_the_e1002_four_line_block (tests/step9_app.rs) is the first test asserting which runtime path actually emits the four-line block for E1002.

feature_name: Streaming JSONL reader enforces line/file/record/nesting bounds to prevent unbounded allocation
user_story: As a user, I want resume reading a maliciously-crafted or actively-growing huge session file to abort bounded, never hang or OOM.
expected_behaviour: `preview::jsonl::Bounds` (DEFAULT_MAX_LINE_BYTES=8MiB, DEFAULT_MAX_FILE_BYTES=512MiB, DEFAULT_MAX_RECORDS=1M, DEFAULT_MAX_NESTING=64) is enforced in `read_buffered` (src/preview/jsonl.rs:122-203): oversized lines are counted and skipped (oversized_lines), a file exceeding the byte bound yields `FileOutcome::BoundExceeded`, the record cap stops enumeration early, and `parse_bounded` rejects JSON nesting deeper than max_nesting.
how_to_test: Craft a fixture with a >8MiB single line and a >512MiB file; confirm read_file returns BoundExceeded and the oversized_lines count, without panicking or exhausting memory.
error_notes: BUG FOUND & FIXED 2026-08-11: read_buffered called reader.read_until(b'\n', &mut line) BEFORE checking payload.len() > max_line_bytes, so the intended 8 MiB line bound only rejected a line AFTER it was already fully buffered — a multi-hundred-MiB/GiB single line would force an allocation of its own size first, defeating the advertised allocation bound. Fixed: new read_line_capped() reads via BufRead::fill_buf/consume directly, never growing its buffer past max_line_bytes+1 regardless of the true line length, while still tracking and reporting the true length so oversized detection is unaffected (src/preview/jsonl.rs). Regression: preview::jsonl::tests::read_line_capped_never_buffers_past_the_cap (directly proves the buffered Vec never exceeds the cap for a line 1000x larger).

feature_name: OMP Active detection staleness gate closes the recycled-TTY false-positive (M3 fix)
user_story: As an OMP user, I want resume to never falsely report a session Active just because a leftover terminal breadcrumb names its path while a DIFFERENT, newer process now owns that recycled TTY — a stale breadcrumb must be rejected against the live process's actual start time.
expected_behaviour: `correlate_live_with` (src/integration/omp/activity.rs:169-211) reads each breadcrumb's `recorded_at` (file mtime, :180-182) and the live process's `started_at` (ProcEntry.started_at, src/proc.rs:35). It rejects the breadcrumb unless fresh: when `started_at` is known, `recorded_at >= started_at` (activity.rs:183-184) — so a breadcrumb written by a PREVIOUS process on that TTY, older than the current process, is dropped. When `started_at` is unavailable it falls back to a 12h `BREADCRUMB_FRESHNESS` window (:192-193) and emits an `OMP_BREADCRUMB_START_TIME_UNAVAILABLE` diagnostic (errors::category::OMP_BREADCRUMB_START_TIME_UNAVAILABLE) so the unknown is surfaced rather than silently trusted. This replaced the pre-fix gate, which was a tautology/no-op: it only checked a `breadcrumb_alive` boolean set without any time comparison, so any recycled-TTY breadcrumb with a live process and matching path falsely reported Active.
how_to_test: Regression test `correlate_live_rejects_breadcrumb_older_than_recycled_tty_process` (src/integration/omp/tests/activity.rs:75): breadcrumb recorded_at = EPOCH, process started_at = EPOCH+1s -> evidence map empty (the exploit is closed). Regression test `missing_process_start_time_uses_twelve_hour_freshness_fallback` (activity.rs:108): started_at=None, breadcrumb at exactly BREADCRUMB_FRESHNESS ago -> Active + 1 diagnostic; 1s older -> empty.
error_notes: Closes docs/review/post-merge-review.md finding M3. Evidence: src/integration/omp/activity.rs:17 (BREADCRUMB_FRESHNESS const), :56-60 (Breadcrumb.recorded_at), :183-195 (freshness gate + fallback diagnostic).

feature_name: Pi discovery tolerates malformed middle records and truncated tails without aborting
user_story: As a Pi user with a partially-corrupt session file, I want resume to salvage valid records rather than skipping the whole file.
expected_behaviour: The shared jsonl reader skips malformed middle records (counted in read.malformed_middle) and marks incomplete tails as IncompleteTail; extract_session retains all valid records parsed before the corruption (src/integration/pi/discover.rs:213-271).
how_to_test: Write a session jsonl with a valid header, a malformed JSON line in the middle, and a valid user message after it; confirm the session still discovers with the valid message.
error_notes: Tests: malformed_middle_record_does_not_abort_discovery (pi/tests/discover.rs:264), truncated_tail_is_incomplete_but_keeps_valid_records (:290).

feature_name: Claude user-message extraction excludes tool_result blocks and injected (isMeta/isSidechain) records from the title summary
user_story: As a Claude Code user, I want session titles to reflect what I actually typed, not tool output or agent-injected sidechain content.
expected_behaviour: interpret_record only treats type="user" records with non-tool_result content and !isMeta/!isSidechain as human input (src/integration/claude/format.rs:100-121, has_human_input :123-137, is_injected :139-148).
how_to_test: Write a transcript with a user record containing only tool_result blocks; confirm it does not contribute to the title. Write one with isMeta=true; confirm it is excluded.
error_notes: Tests: user_record_with_only_tool_result_blocks_is_excluded_from_title (claude/tests/format.rs:224), mixed_text_and_tool_result_blocks_extract_human_text_only (:258), assistant_system_and_injected_records_excluded_from_user_messages (:290). Citation update (2026-08-11 real-binary QA pass): Cite src/integration/claude/format.rs:121-169.

feature_name: Claude discovery never modifies any file, directory, or mtime
user_story: As a Claude Code user, I want resume's discovery to be purely read-only so it cannot corrupt my session store.
expected_behaviour: discover() and collect_candidates only read directories and open files for reading; no file is opened for write, no directory entry or mtime is changed (src/integration/claude/discover.rs:37-41 doc comment).
how_to_test: Snapshot all file mtimes and contents under a Claude config root before and after `resume --list --agent claude`; confirm zero changes.
error_notes: Test: discovery_does_not_modify_any_file_or_directory (claude/tests/discover.rs:329).

feature_name: Claude discovery emits claude_truncated, claude_oversized, and claude_malformed non-fatal diagnostics while retaining valid sessions
user_story: As a Claude Code user diagnosing with --verbose, I want to know when a transcript was truncated, oversized, or had malformed middle records, without losing the session entirely.
expected_behaviour: parse_candidate pushes nonfatal diagnostics for IncompleteTail (claude_truncated), BoundExceeded (claude_oversized), and malformed_middle > 0 (claude_malformed), but still returns Some(session) (src/integration/claude/format.rs:268-289).
how_to_test: Write a transcript ending mid-JSON-line; confirm claude_truncated appears and the session is retained. Write one exceeding the read bound; confirm claude_oversized. Write one with a malformed middle line; confirm claude_malformed.
error_notes: Tests: truncated_incomplete_tail_is_diagnosed_but_session_retained (claude/tests/format.rs:341), malformed_middle_record_is_diagnosed_but_not_aborted (:375). Citation update (2026-08-11 real-binary QA pass): Cite src/integration/claude/format.rs:283-317.

feature_name: Git common-dir lookup is memoized per canonical Workspace (performance contract)
user_story: As a user resuming inside a large repo with many sessions, I want resume to query each Workspace's git common directory at most once, so discovery stays fast rather than spawning one git subprocess per session.
expected_behaviour: In ScopeMode::Git, Scope::contains_workspace resolves git_common_dir via cached_git_common_dir (src/scope.rs:155-179), keyed by canonical path, shared via Arc<Scope> across per-agent threads. Non-Git modes skip the spawn entirely (src/scope.rs:142).
how_to_test: Run contains_workspace against the same canonical path repeatedly and confirm only the first call spawns git.
error_notes: Test: contains_workspace_memoizes_git_common_dir_per_canonical_path (src/scope.rs) asserts the second batch of identical-path calls is >=5x faster than the first. Implements docs/product-design.md §4 'Query each normalized Workspace at most once.'

feature_name: A Session whose Workspace was deleted is still Scope-matched via its last-known real path
user_story: As a user, I want a session recorded under a now-deleted directory to still be matched by Scope (so it appears, marked Unavailable) rather than silently vanishing from the list.
expected_behaviour: resolve_missing_workspace_path (src/scope.rs:198-219) canonicalizes the nearest existing ancestor and re-appends the missing suffix; contains_workspace falls back to it when canonicalize fails (src/scope.rs:136-150).
how_to_test: Discover a session under /real/base/deleted (base exists, deleted subdir does not); confirm it is still matched under --down all, while an unrelated /other/deleted path is not.
error_notes: Test: missing_workspace_uses_its_last_known_path_for_scope_matching (src/scope.rs). Distinct from scope-unavailable-workspace (which marks availability); this row pins the Scope-membership contract for deleted paths.

feature_name: Config parse errors report file path, line/column, and offending field
user_story: As a user with a typo in config.toml, I want the error to name the file, line, and field so I can fix it without guessing.
expected_behaviour: ConfigError::Parse interpolates {source} (the toml::de::Error Display carrying line/column + field) alongside {path:?} (src/config.rs:56-60), so the message includes 'line 1' and the field name.
how_to_test: Write config.toml containing `mystery = true`; run `resume --config <path> --list`; confirm the error contains 'line 1' and 'mystery'.
error_notes: Test: parse_error_message_includes_line_and_field_detail (src/config.rs:158). Implements docs/product-design.md §7 'errors with file/line/column when possible.'

feature_name: Interactive picker waits for Pi/OMP/Claude before opening; Codex discovers in the background
user_story: As a user with many discovered sessions, I want a single, stable, correctly-sorted view without waiting on whichever agent happens to be slowest -- observed on a real corpus: Pi/OMP/Claude finish in well under 200ms, Codex can take 18+ seconds.
expected_behaviour: `run_interactive` splits configured agents into sync (everything but Codex) and, when at least one other agent is also configured, async (Codex alone). Sync agent threads are joined as before (one `resume: <agent> scanned (<elapsed>)` progress line per agent to stderr, in real completion order) before the Picker opens. Codex's thread is spawned but never joined before opening the Picker; it merges its records into the same `Arc<Mutex<Vec<PickerCandidate>>>` the Picker reads (`merge_records`) whenever it finishes, and its own progress line is buffered and printed only after the Picker returns (never mid-render, since Skim owns the terminal). `picker::run_tabbed_picker` takes an optional `BackgroundAgent { label, pending }` and shows a `(codex still scanning)` header hint while it runs. When Codex is the only configured agent it stays synchronous (src/app.rs run_interactive, merge_records; src/picker.rs run_tabbed_picker, BackgroundAgent).
how_to_test: Run `resume` from a real Scope where Codex's corpus is large; observe the Picker opens within ~1s showing Pi/OMP/Claude's Sessions and a `(codex still scanning)` header hint, well before Codex would traditionally finish. After Codex finishes, switch tabs (Alt+Left/Alt+Right) and confirm a `codex` tab appears with its Sessions and the hint clears. Exit (Esc) and confirm `resume: codex scanned (<elapsed>)` prints after the Picker's screen is gone, with a clean (non-corrupted) render throughout.
error_notes: Tests: tabbed_picker_opens_immediately_while_background_agent_scans, tabbed_picker_paginates_and_switches_tabs (tests/picker_spike.rs). Real-corpus smoke test (Codex 3546 rollouts / 2.7GB, Scope with 1016+ matching Sessions): Picker opened in 629-738ms with `(codex still scanning)` shown; `resume: codex scanned (18.23s)` printed cleanly after Esc, matching the originally reported 19.14s real-world timing this change targets.

feature_name: Picker presents an All tab plus one tab per agent; Alt+P/Alt+N page, Alt+Left/Alt+Right switch tabs
user_story: As a user, I want to browse all sessions together (All) or narrow to one agent (a per-agent tab), and within either view page through more than 50 sessions, using simple keys.
expected_behaviour: `run_tabbed_picker` builds tabs as `All` (index 0) plus one tab per distinct `PickerCandidate.agent`, in first-seen order after the global ascending sort; each tab is independently paginated at `PAGE_SIZE` (50), defaulting to its newest page. `Alt+P`/`Alt+N` (`classify_nav`, `SkimKey::Alt('p')`/`Alt('n')`) move pages within the current tab, only bound when that direction exists. `Alt+Left`/`Alt+Right` (`SkimKey::AltLeft`/`AltRight`) cycle tabs with wraparound and reset to the target tab's newest page. Every page turn or tab switch relaunches a small, fresh Skim instance over just that slice (src/picker.rs run_tabbed_picker, run_single_view, build_tabbed_options, classify_nav).
how_to_test: With 3+ agents and one agent having 50+ sessions: from the All tab's last page, press Alt+P and confirm the header reads a lower page number and the newest-page-only session disappears; press Alt+Left/Alt+Right and confirm the header's bracketed tab name changes and cycling wraps past the last tab back to All; confirm Enter still resolves the correct session from whichever tab/page is active.
error_notes: Test: tabbed_picker_paginates_and_switches_tabs (tests/picker_spike.rs) — 120-session, 4-tab, multi-page PTY end-to-end scenario.

feature_name: Codex discovery uses up to 8 bounded worker threads instead of scanning one file at a time
user_story: As a user with a large Codex rollout store, I want discovery to finish quickly even on a corpus much bigger than my current Scope, since Codex's store has no per-directory Workspace pruning to shrink the file list before reading.
expected_behaviour: discover_with_filter_enriched splits each root's file list across up to MAX_DISCOVERY_WORKERS=8 scoped threads (parallel_map; falls back to sequential below PARALLEL_THRESHOLD=16 files to avoid thread-spawn overhead on small corpora), reassembling results in original sorted order before any downstream code (filter, sqlite enrichment, Session construction) sees them -- output is unaffected by the parallelism, only wall-clock time (src/integration/codex/discover.rs parallel_map, discover_with_filter_enriched).
how_to_test: Time `resume --agent codex --json <dir>` against a real large Codex corpus (hundreds+ rollouts) with a cold cache; observe wall time close to `user+sys` CPU time divided across cores rather than serial. Compare stdout against a small-corpus (<16 files, forces the sequential fallback) run for parity.
error_notes: Real-corpus measurement (3546 rollouts / 2.9GB): in-process 8-worker read of 1200 files took 0.086s vs 1.2s serial (14x). Cold full corpus scan (1016-session Scope) took 3.95s, matching or beating the pre-parallelism single-threaded baseline (up to 18-19s observed on the same corpus under real invocation).

feature_name: Codex discovery cache: reuse an unchanged rollout's parsed content across runs
user_story: As a user who runs resume repeatedly against the same machine's Codex sessions (often from different project directories over time), I want repeat invocations to skip re-reading and re-parsing rollout files that have not changed.
expected_behaviour: codex::cache::DiscoveryCache loads a JSON file at $XDG_CACHE_HOME/resume/codex-discovery-v1.json (falling back to ~/.cache/resume/; codex::cache::cache_path) keyed by each rollout's canonical absolute path, storing (size, mtime, parsed-content-or-no-session). A lookup hit (matching size+mtime) skips the file read and JSON parse entirely; a miss does a full, ungated parse (bypassing the Scope Workspace-gate, since a gate rejection is Scope-specific and must never be cached as a durable 'no session' fact) and records the result. The cache is purely non-authoritative: a missing/corrupt/version-mismatched file loads as empty (never an error), a write failure is silently swallowed, and deleting the file is always safe -- the rollout JSONL remains the source of truth. SQLite enrichment hints are never cached; they are recomputed fresh on every run on top of the cached-or-parsed content (src/integration/codex/cache.rs; src/integration/codex/discover.rs parse_for_discovery) On save, an entry whose path falls under the current run's effective_root but was not observed this run (the file no longer exists) is pruned as an orphan -- dynamic, run-driven garbage collection with no separate sweep job, since caching guarantees every currently-existing file under that root is always seen. An entry under a *different* effective_root (a different CODEX_HOME from an earlier run) is never pruned, since this run has no evidence about a root it did not scan (DiscoveryCache::save).
how_to_test: Run `resume --agent codex --json <dir>` twice against the same real Scope with the same $XDG_CACHE_HOME; diff the two JSON outputs (must be byte-identical) and observe the second run is dramatically faster. Modify a rollout file's content and confirm its cached entry is invalidated (next run re-parses it). Delete the cache file and confirm the next run degrades gracefully to a full fresh scan with identical output Delete a rollout file between two runs against the same CODEX_HOME/XDG_CACHE_HOME and confirm its cache entry is gone after the second run's save; confirm an entry cached under a *different* CODEX_HOME in an earlier run survives untouched.
error_notes: Unit tests: src/integration/codex/cache.rs (9 tests: hit/miss/staleness-after-modification/corrupt-file/version-mismatch/persists-across-load-save-load/pathless-in-run-only). Integration test: integration::codex::tests::cached_and_uncached_discovery_produce_identical_sessions. Real-corpus measurement: cold (populating cache) 3.95s -> warm 0.17-0.19s (20-23x), byte-identical JSON output confirmed via diff on both a scoped (1016-session) and full-corpus run Plus 2 dedicated pruning tests: save_prunes_an_entry_for_a_file_deleted_since_it_was_cached, save_never_prunes_entries_under_a_different_effective_root. End-to-end verified against the real release binary with a synthetic 2-file corpus: entries 2 -> delete one file -> rerun -> entries 1.

feature_name: Codex JSON workspace field matches other agents (no silent symlink resolution)
user_story: As a user consuming resume --json across multiple agents in the same real project directory, I want the workspace field for the same real directory to render identically regardless of which agent recorded the session, so I can group/dedupe sessions across agents by workspace.
expected_behaviour: resolve_workspace_cwd (src/integration/codex/discover.rs, renamed from canonicalize_workspace) now keeps an absolute recorded cwd verbatim, exactly like Claude/Pi/OMP's WorkspaceEvidence -- it no longer calls Path::canonicalize() to resolve symlinks. Scope membership (scope::contains_workspace) still canonicalizes its own copy for matching, so Scope/Directory-Distance filtering is unaffected; only the value stored in Session.workspace and surfaced via --json/--list changes. A relative cwd is still dropped (None), unchanged from before.
how_to_test: Under a symlinked base directory (e.g. macOS /tmp -> /private/tmp), record one session per agent with the identical recorded cwd string, run `resume --json`, and confirm every agent's workspace field is byte-identical.
error_notes: 2026-08-23 audit: live docs/qa/fixtures.sh run under macOS (whose $TMPDIR is under the /var -> /private/var symlink) showed Codex's workspace field as /private/var/folders/... while Claude/Pi/OMP's was /var/folders/... for the identical recorded cwd -- confirmed via direct code reading (codex's canonicalize_workspace called .canonicalize(), the other three integrations store parsed.cwd verbatim) and reproduced against the compiled binary. Contradicts docs/product-design.md Sec 3's contract that Preview's separate 'canonical real path' field, not the workspace identity field, carries symlink resolution. Fixed by removing the .canonicalize() call for the existing-absolute-path case; codex's 86 unit tests (all of which already write pre-canonicalized cwd into fixtures) and the full cargo test --all-features --locked suite (496 passed) plus make ci passed unchanged. Re-verified live: all four agents' --json workspace strings now identical for the same real directory.
